Serve as the Technical Point of Contact
- Serve as DEFCON AI’s technical point of contact for the customer and industry partner
- Work closely with the Program Manager on scope, schedule, risk, and status reporting
- Own the technical increment plan from pilot through production and confirm the scope and acceptance criteria for each increment with the customer before work begins
- Track and drive government-side technical prerequisites, including accounts, access, approvals, and authorization

Own Cloud Platform Architecture and Delivery
- Own the architecture for deploying containerized services into a secure government cloud environment
- Lead cloud networking, identity, and hardened deployment, while ensuring the pilot is built on a baseline that can carry into production
- Work with partner engineering teams on hosting and integration and evaluate hosting options with clear recommended courses of action

Lead Data Integration and Decision Support
- Lead the integration of customer data sources into the delivered capability
- Shape decision-support views with the customer’s operations staff, including mapping, prediction, and alerting
- Partner with the Program Manager to define success measures with the customer before implementation and report results that inform decisions about the next

Riot is building the capabilities to carry AI and machine learning from promise, through prototype, into reliable production systems. AI Foundations helps make that possible by building shared platforms and enabling teams across Riot to deliver meaningful AI-powered outcomes.

We are looking for an engineering leader to oversee the AI Foundations engineering organization. You will be accountable for the technical impact of the group including organizational health, operational excellence, software and machine learning craft quality, and engineering output. All Engineering Managers in AI Foundations will report into this role.

You will partner with product and executive leaders to connect Riot’s goals to a clear charter, long-term roadmap, and investment choices. The role calls for an organization-level leader who stays technically engaged: close enough to understand the engineering realities, guide important decisions, and address risks, while creating the clarity and space for managers and teams to lead execution.

SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the team

The IT team supports SambaNova’s employees and infrastructure. We manage the servers, networks, and cloud accounts our engineering teams use to build and test AI chips and systems. We also handle employee laptops, accounts, and software, and we run security across the company. The team is small and works closely with engineering and DevOps.

As Director of IT on the IT team, you will lead infrastructure, end-user IT, security operations, and DevOps support across the company. You will set the direction for the function and grow the team, and you will also do hands-on work when the team needs it. At Senra Systems, we believe that the future of manufacturing lies not in automation, but in configuration.

We supercharge electrical wire harness manufacturing through software configuration, transforming skilled assembly tasks into high-throughput production lines. We enable customers to design what they want, when they want it and deliver harness builds at record-breaking speed.

The Head of Engineering leads Senra Systems' Manufacturing and Industrial Engineering teams and sets the engineering vision, standards, and execution behind every wire harness and cable assembly we build for our aerospace customers. This leader builds on Senra's established practices to formalize, standardize, and continuously improve our engineering processes, documentation, and team structure as the company grows. Working closely with the Head of Production and the Head of Manufacturing Excellence & Training, this role designs and scales the processes that drive consistent, high-quality production. This role is central to delivering the quality, reliability, and on-time performance aerospace programs demand, and to positioning Senra as a trusted name in aerospace interconnect manufacturing.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Lead and scale the Engineering organization, owning manufacturing engineering, industrial engineering, new product introduction (NPI), and sustaining engineering across all programs.

• Assess existing processes, documentation, and team structure, then define and standardize them into a clear engineering system, including work instructions, routings, BOMs, drawing standards, ECN/ECO change control, and document control.

• Own the NPI process from customer drawings through first article inspection (AS9102) and production release, so new programs launch on time and at quality.

• Partner closely with the Head of Production and the Head of Manufacturing Excellence & Training to design, implement, and scale manufacturing processes, making sure engineering standards, work instructions, and process changes translate into consistent execution on the floor and effective operator training.

• Drive manufacturing excellence through line design, capacity planning, labor standards, time studies, tooling and equipment strategy, and Lean and continuous improvement practices.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

DIRECTOR, SECURITY, INVESTIGATIONS AND INTELLIGENCE

Help protect people, intellectual property, platforms, financial systems, facilities, and national-security work across X, X Money, SpaceXSI, and SpaceX. The Director of Security, Investigations and Intelligence leads investigations, intelligence, security screenings, and counterintelligence, and serves as the Insider Threat Program Senior Official. The role requires deep investigative experience and technical credibility with the teams that run detection engineering and digital forensics. Ideal candidates have run a cleared insider threat program, led investigative teams, and worked with law enforcement and government partners.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Lead internal and external investigations across X, X Money, SpaceXSI, and SpaceX, including insider threat, employee and contractor misconduct, intellectual property theft, data exfiltration, fraud, platform abuse, and financial crime
- Set investigative direction for X, including the integrity of agents on the platform (automated or AI-driven accounts and actions), account compromise caused by insider misuse, support to operations that disrupt threat actors, and influence operations
- Oversee X Money financial-crime investigations in support of Bank Secrecy Act and anti-money-laundering obligations, including suspicious activity reports made with the financial-crimes team
- Direct the intelligence and counterintelligence programs, including collection, analysis, production, dissemination, adversary tracking, and supply-chain and third-party risk
- Own required reporting, including adverse information reports, suspicious contact reports to the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), security incident inquiries, and counterintelligence referrals to the FBI or DCSA
- Partner with Program Security Officers, government customers, and DCSA, and prepare the program for DCSA security reviews
- Direct high-side investigations, including user activity monitoring on classified networks, classified data-spill response, storage of case files and evidence inside a SCIF, and classified chain of custody

DIRECTOR, MATERIALS MANAGEMENT (STARBASE INFRASTRUCTURE - LOUISIANA)

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

We are seeking a hands-on, results-driven leader to own materials management operations for the Starship Program at our new Louisiana site. This role is responsible for standing up and leading materials operations; Including receiving, inventory management, material handling, kitting, and lineside delivery in support of Starship production. The director will build the organization, systems, and material flow required for a new site, then scale them as production rate increases. The director will drive operational excellence, safety, inventory accuracy, flight-hardware traceability, and productivity while developing a high-performing team of hourly and salaried employees. The ideal candidate will have a successful track record of leading large teams, managing complex operations, and building productive working relationships across manufacturing, supply chain, engineering, quality, and launch operations. This position is based in Starbase, Texas (Brownsville/South Padre Island Area) until early 2027. At that time, relocation to Louisiana will be required.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Own the end-to-end materials management strategy and day-to-day operations for Starbase, LA, including shipping and receiving, inventory management, material handling, kitting, production-line support, and on-site logistics as the new Starship site comes online and ramps
- Stand up materials processes for Starship production, covering large structures, propulsion hardware, avionics, thermal protection, ground support equipment, and the high part mix, serialization, and traceability those commodities require
- Lead inbound and outbound logistics, truck and yard operations, and material-flow design so the right hardware arrives on time and in the right condition for production, integration, and test
- Define and execute the site materials operating system for a new facility: layout, storage strategy, handling methods for oversized and heavy flight hardware, and the controls that protect inventory accuracy from day one
- Drive capital planning, automation roadmaps, and process design — including WMS and ERP integration and material-handling solutions appropriate to Starship hardware — to improve velocity, accuracy, and cost as rate increases
- Establish and own site materials KPIs, inventory health, cost, and operational metrics aligned with Starship product

We're building healthcare tech for a system that desperately needs it.

Each year, millions of Americans deal with confusing changes to their Medicare plans that impact their prescriptions, access to care, and pocketbooks. These aren’t just inconveniences – they are potentially life-altering changes that leave seniors medically and financially vulnerable.

Independent Medicare advisors play a crucial role in guiding seniors through this complexity and helping them find the right coverage for their needs. But their ability to be effective healthcare advocates has long been hamstrung by broken tools and outdated systems.

Spark is fixing that. We’re the fastest-growing Medicare platform in the country, combining AI, an industry-leading CRM, and client services to transform how 10,000+ brokers acquire, enroll, and support clients in their local communities.

Healthcare is overdue for innovation. Let’s redefine what its future looks like — together.

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable—unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Each runs on purpose-built process skids that our team designs, procures, builds, and commissions.

The Director of Fuel Equipment Engineering owns the design of that equipment end to end: from early skid design through to fabrication, factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning, and handover to fuel production operations.

About Valar Atomics

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable—unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Our first pilot plant in Orangeville, Utah will demonstrate how advanced nuclear systems and fuel fabrication can power the future. Joining Valar Atomics means becoming part of a company where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level.

The Team

The Numenor team is building Valar’s next reactor, the flagship program that will define how we deliver nuclear power at scale. This dedicated team owns the entire plant, from the reactor core and helium systems to cooling, plant modules, and the Citadel, uniting mechanical, systems, safety, IC&E, quality, and supply chain under one mission. The work starts with bringing the first unit to life and ends with a production line that delivers reactors faster with every build. What this team builds will power the critical infrastructure of the future.

The Role

Valar Atomics seeks a Director, Systems Engineering for the reactor program. This role will build and lead the systems engineering organization for the reactor program. The scope covers the systems engineering process, the product breakdown structure (PBS), and the structure and technical accuracy of the reactor design basis. The role will lead systems integration and engineering from the first unit through scaled production, delivering reactors at an increasing rate.

The role demands someone who can develop, implement, and maintain a systems engineering architecture and high-value tools that enable Valar to produce and license Numenor series reactors at scale. - Own the V&V strategy, from requirement to evidence, through factory test, integrated test, and commissioning, working closely with the test director and test team.

Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) accelerates digital transformation so customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. The Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform protects thousands of customers from cyberattacks and data loss by securely connecting users, devices, and applications in any location. Distributed across 200+ public data centers globally and thousands of private sites at the edge, the SASE-based Zero Trust Exchange is the world’s largest in-line cloud security platform.

We believe the future of work is Human + AI and are building an AI-native enterprise where human potential is amplified by machine intelligence to solve the world’s hardest security challenges. Driven by deep customer obsession, we are committed to the mission, outcome, and to each other. We bring these commitments to life through three core behaviors: ownership and collaboration, trust through outcomes and impact, and a challenge culture with ongoing feedback. Ready to make an impact at the company pioneering security transformation in the AI era? Join us at Zscaler.

Role

As the Senior Director, MSSP , you will join our Channel and Alliances team and report directly to the SVP of Global Channels.

In this executive-level leadership role, you will own the commercial strategy, operational execution, and revenue quota for Zscaler's low- and no-touch sales, managed security service provider (MSSP), distribution, and aggregator business. You will build highly productive partner relationships and establish repeatable, partner-led sales motions that drive customer acquisition, expansion, and recurring revenue while drastically improving overall global sales efficiency.

Who You Are
- You thrive in ambiguity. You're comfortable building the path as you walk it. You thrive in a dynamic environment, seeing ambiguity not as a hindrance, but as the raw material to build something meaningful.
- You act like an owner. Your passion for the mission fuels your bias for action. You operate with integrity because you genuinely care about the outcome. True ownership involves leveraging dynamic range: the ability to navigate seamlessly between high-level strategy and hands-on execution.

This is a rare opportunity to join a team that is bringing an entirely new category of brain health to the world. At Cognito, we are developing therapies designed to promote dignity, clarity, and coherence in the lives they touch.

Cognito is a neurotechnology company developing a new therapeutic approach to cognitive and neurological health, designed to work with the brain's own activity and biology. Born from pioneering neuroscience research at MIT, Cognito brings together neuroscience, engineering, medicine and technology to translate breakthroughs in brain science into practical therapies designed for everyday life.

Our first therapeutic application, Spectris AD, is an investigational, prescription, at-home therapy for Alzheimer's disease. With our pivotal HOPE study now complete, Cognito is entering an important new phase as we advance Spectris AD toward regulatory review, prepare for potential commercialization and continue exploring the broader potential of our science across neurological health.

We are building an interdisciplinary team united by a shared purpose: protecting and progressing the human ability to think, learn and remember. For innovators who want to work at the intersection of breakthrough science, technology and human health, Cognito offers the chance to help shape what comes next.
About The Job

Cognito is building a Security, Privacy, and IT organization from the ground up under the SVP of Security, Privacy, and IT, structured across three functions. The Information Security Director leads the Information Security function day-to-day — hiring and running the team, and driving SOC 2 and HIPAA audit readiness to completion, with HITRUST in the future — under the strategic direction of the SVP, who holds overall executive (CISO-level) accountability for security.
Responsibilities

Build & Lead the Information Security Function
• Stand up and run Information Security day-to-day: hire and manage a team.
• Set team goals and performance expectations as the function grows through 2028.
Certification & Audit Readiness
• Drive SOC 2 and HIPAA audit preparation and execution end-to-end — scoping, control implementation, evidence collection, and auditor coordination.
• Build toward the multi-year HITRUST certification goal, reporting progress and risk up to the SVP.
Policy, Risk & Vendor Management
• Build and maintain the information security policy set (access control, data protection, vendor risk, incident response, etc) that the rest of the team will operate against.
• Establish a vendor security review process for new tools and vendors as the company scales.
Client & Partner Security Support
• Serve as the day-to-day technical security contact in partner and client diligence conversations, escalating to the SVP for executive-level or strategic discussions.
Interim Leadership & Team Growth
• Provide an interim reporting home for the Privacy Analyst, until the Privacy Director is hired.
• Hire and ramp the Security team.

Role overview

Lead the design and hands-on rebuild of cloud, delivery, and AI infrastructure supporting customer-facing products and venue operations. The role combines strategic platform decisions with implementation, setting standards that product and corporate engineering teams can use to ship reliably and operate services with clear ownership.
Responsibilities
• Replace manual releases with an automated CI/CD path covering builds, deployment, and rollback.
• Define and migrate source control, CI, orchestration, and infrastructure-as-code practices; document key trade-offs.
• Establish access controls, audit trails, secrets handling, environment separation, and practical recovery procedures.
• Build and operate an AI gateway for provider routing, credentials, rate limits, usage metering, and logging.
• Enable AI-assisted, specification-led development with episodic environments, rapid feedback, and automated checks.
• Track cloud and AI costs, improve observability and incident ownership, and support applications used by venue networking teams.
Requirements
• At least nine years building and operating production cloud infrastructure.
• Deep AWS experience, including multi-account environments, networking, IAM, and EKS and/or ECS.
• Experience handling production incidents, upgrades, and growth.
• Ability to communicate technical decisions and trade-offs to engineering, business, and executive audiences.
• A collaborative approach to code review, pairing, mentoring, and sharing operational knowledge.
• Practical use of AI agents for multi-step work, with the ability to verify their output against real systems.
Benefits and work setup

The position is described as hands-on, highly autonomous, and without direct reports listed base salary range is $180,000–$220,000, with a stated total rewards range of $198,000–$242,000 including an annual performance bonus. Benefits include health coverage, paid time off, parental leave, retirement matching, and education support.

About Us

We are Digital Science and we are advancing the research ecosystem.

We are a pioneering technology company, and our vision is of a future where a trusted and collaborative research ecosystem drives progress for all. We believe in better, open, collaborative and inclusive research. In creating the next generation of tools and working in partnership with the community we tackle some of the biggest challenges to research. In order to achieve our vision, we need innovative, inspiring and dynamic people to join our team. Want to join us?

Your new role

DS has grown through acquisition, and its products, data and engineering practices have grown up separately. This role leads the move from that fragmented portfolio to one platform: a single data platform and shared services that every DS product builds on, run by engineering teams working to a consistent operating model.

The VP owns engineering best practice across the group, defines and rolls out a single Target Operating Model (TOM) for engineering, and leads the transformation of today's operating model onto it. The role also owns the foundational layers of the platform (data platform, identity and access, logging, licensing and other shared services) and is accountable for their adoption by product and engineering teams.

The core challenge is to make the whole greater than the sum of its parts. Products should share data, services and standards, while current customer commitments and revenue-critical data releases stay dependable through the transition. Success means a trusted, reusable and commercially valuable data foundation, less duplicated capability, and faster, more consistent delivery across DS.

The VP also works with the Chief AI Officer to deliver the AI plan, and manages the transition of DS engineering to an AI-first software development lifecycle (SDLC).

What you’ll be doing

Engineering strategy and operating model

• Define and own engineering best practice across the group, covering architecture, data architecture, quality, infrastructure and FinOps.
• Design a single, consistent Target Operating Model for all engineering, and lead the transformation of the current operating model onto it.
• Agree an incremental platform roadmap with product leadership, with visible dependencies, early wins and clear progress measures.
• Lead adoption as well as build: agree integration paths with product teams, reduce duplicated capability and retire legacy components.
• Lead the rollout of an AI-first operating model across engineering, setting standards for AI-enabled development practices.

Unified data platform

• Deliver one data platform that underpins all DS applications and brings together data sources from across the group.
• Consolidate duplicated ingestion implementations onto a shared ingestion capability with common standards.
• Establish enrichment as a reusable platform capability, with clear ownership and a route to modernise long-standing algorithms and processes.

jsearch:lumira search:UFg0ZmhreGxfY0NKSj.description:
Lumira Search is partnered with a medtech start-up developing next-generation cardiovascular devices. Our client has a commercial product line in endovascular, and clinical stage transcatheter heart valve program.

This is a pivotal moment for the company, having recently vertically integrated manufacturing and closing a large finance round, they are consolidating into a new purpose-built facility in the Philadelphia area and restructuring into focused product divisions, each with dedicated leadership and the backing of an in-house manufacturing and development organisation.
The Role:

We’re looking to recruit technical leader to head R&D for the company's heart valve division. Think of this as leading a standalone valve start-up: you’ll act as the technical founder and CTO of the division, owning the development program end to end while building and leading a team of 5–10 engineers and scientists.

You’ll work alongside internal manufacturing, quality and regulatory functions, giving you the speed of a start-up with the infrastructure that most early-stage companies don’t have.
Responsibilities:
• Lead the technical strategy and execution of the clinical-stage surgical and transcatheter valve program
• Build, mentor and lead a high-performing R&D team of 5–10 people
• Drive design, verification and validation activities through clinical and regulatory milestones
• Partner closely with quality, regulatory, operations and manufacturing to move the program toward commercialisation
• Shape the culture, processes and long-term roadmap of a newly formed division
What We’re Looking For
• 10–15 years of medical device R&D experience, with strong experience in transcatheter heart valves
• Hands-on experience through one or more full product development cycles
• Proven people leadership and ready to step up
• Strong technical depth combined with the ability to set direction and make decisions in an early-stage environment
• Experience with polymer-based implants is a strong advantage
Why Join:
• A genuine founder-style leadership role with significant ownership and impact
• Competitive salary and benefits
• The chance to help bring a novel valve technology to patients

Location: This role is fully on-site at in the Philadelphia metro area.

Please note:

Whilst I'd like to respond to all candidates, due to the anticipated high volume of applicants I am simply unable to. If you do not meet the above requirements and haven't heard from me within 14 days of applying, please assume your application was unsuccessful.
jsearch:lumira search:UFg0ZmhreGxfY0NKSj.title: Chief Technology Officer

Fast-Growing, Profitable Tech Startup

MedFlo AI is an independent technology organization built in close partnership with one of the nation’s leading healthcare companies. Our AI-powered systems are transforming how healthcare facilities process and manage data.

We’re profitable and fast-growing.

Due to company expansion, we are looking for an exceptional, hands-on CTO to lead our technology, engineering, and product development as we scale to the next level.

We need a fast-moving, highly technical leader who thinks like a founder, executes quickly, understands product deeply, and can turn complex ideas into scalable solutions.

What We're Looking For
• Expert in Python, including modern Python frameworks (FastAPI, Django, Flask).
• Strong React experience, with a deep understanding of frontend architecture and UI/UX design.
• Full-stack technical leadership — capable of architecting systems, writing code, and leading engineering teams.
• Extremely fast-paced and execution-driven — someone who moves quickly, solves problems, and gets things shipped.
• Exceptional product instincts — understands both the technical and business sides of building great products.
• Startup mentality — resourceful, entrepreneurial, hands-on, and comfortable taking full ownership.
• Healthcare technology experience is a major plus.

This is not a traditional management role. We're looking for a technical powerhouse and strategic leader who can build, lead, innovate, and help take an already profitable, growing company to the next level.

This position is based in our Ocean County, NJ office. An in-office schedule is required, though a hybrid arrangement may be considered. A competitive relocation package may also be offered for the right candidate.

Employees of MedFlo AI enjoy competitive compensation and benefits aligned with MedFlo’s own plans—reflecting our commitment to rewarding innovation, technical excellence, and impact within a dynamic and fast-growing environment.

We’re profitable and fast-growing.

Due to company expansion, we are looking for an exceptional, hands-on CTO to lead our technology, engineering, and product development as we scale to the next level.

We need a fast-moving, highly technical leader who thinks like a founder, executes quickly, understands product deeply, and can turn complex ideas into scalable solutions.
What We're Looking For
• Expert in Python
, including modern Python frameworks (FastAPI, Django, Flask).
• Strong React experience
, with a deep understanding of frontend architecture and UI/UX design.
• Full-stack technical leadership — capable of architecting systems, writing code, and leading engineering teams.
• Extremely fast-paced and execution-driven — someone who moves quickly, solves problems, and gets things shipped.
• Exceptional product instincts — understands both the technical and business sides of building great products.
• Startup mentality — resourceful, entrepreneurial, hands-on, and comfortable taking full ownership.
• Healthcare technology experience is a major plus.

This is not a traditional management role. We're looking for a technical powerhouse and strategic leader who can build, lead, innovate, and help take an already profitable, growing company to the next level.

This position is based in our Ocean County, NJ office. An in-office schedule is required, though a hybrid arrangement may be considered. A competitive relocation package may also be offered for the right candidate.

Employees of Med Flo AI enjoy competitive compensation and benefits aligned with Med Flo’s own plans—reflecting our commitment to rewarding innovation, technical excellence, and impact within a dynamic and fast-growing environment.

ABOUT NEQ OPERATING

NEQ Operating is a leading operator of upstream oil and gas assets across the Lower 48, managing a diversified, multi-basin portfolio that includes assets in South Texas, Haynesville and the Mid-Continent. Backed by Quantum Capital Group and NextEra Energy Resources, NEQ is building a scaled, world-class upstream business through the strategic acquisition, development and optimization of PDP-heavy, yield-oriented assets.
ROLE SUMMARY

The Director, Information Technology is NEQ’s senior technology and data leader and a key member of the executive leadership team, reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer. The role owns executing the technology agenda for an independent upstream operator: strategic partnerships, business applications, data and analytics, AI, infrastructure and cloud, field and operational technology, end-user devices and cybersecurity.

NEQ treats data and technology as a strategic asset. This leader will build a lean, high-performing function, with leads for Data/Analytics/AI, Operational Technology / Engineering Technology (OT/ET) and IT, that turns operational, subsurface, land and financial data into faster and better-informed decisions, using a deliberate blend of in-house talent and best-in-class partners. The role is equal parts strategist, builder and operator. This position is based in Houston, Texas or Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Technology and data strategy: Develop and own a multi-year technology and data strategy and roadmap aligned to NEQ’s operating plan, development program, capital discipline and continuous optimization of the business; serve as the COO’s principal advisor on technology, data and digital opportunities.

• Governance and value: Establish technology and data governance, including project portfolio prioritization, architecture standards and decision rights with business leaders; build business cases and cost/benefit analyses, and report on realized value.

• Data foundation: Lead the design of a trusted, well-governed data platform that integrates drilling and completions, production, subsurface, land, marketing and financial data into a single, authoritative version of the truth, with data ownership, quality standards and master data management for wells, properties, owners, vendors, contracts and AFEs.

• Decision support: Partner with Operations, Subsurface, Land, Engineering and Finance as co-owners of analytics priorities, delivering self-service reporting, dashboards and advanced analytics, such as production surveillance, cost per well and capital performance.

• AI and automation: Work hand in hand with business domain leaders to evaluate and responsibly deploy AI, machine learning and automation where they create measurable operational or financial value.

• Business applications: Own the upstream application portfolio, including ERP and financials, revenue and joint interest accounting, production accounting, land and division order systems,

The company designs, develops, and operates hospitality-driven destinations to host gatherings of all kinds, ranging from small corporate meetings to immersive brand activations and beyond. We love bringing people together in person, and that passion for great experiences extends to our employees as well.

If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team.
Director, Cloud Infrastructure

We're hiring a Director of Cloud Infrastructure to join Convene Hospitality Group's (CHG) Technology organization. It's a hands-on role with an AI-native mindset. There are no direct reports today. You’ll lead through the platform, redesigning how we deploy and setting the standards our product and corporate engineering teams build on. Legacy migration follows the decisions. You make the call, then you do the move. This role will have a lot of influence.

This is a wide seat. You’ll work across product and corporate engineering, and you’re a big part of how we get to AI-first, spec-driven development.

When Paleovalley co-founders Autumn and Chas Smith saw how industrialized food was affecting human health and the health of the land, they refused to play along. Autumn’s own journey of healing through nutrient-dense foods lit a fire that became Paleovalley. From there, the mission grew roots, sprouted wings, and eventually expanded into Wild Pastures to bring regeneratively raised meats directly to families nationwide.

Today, Paleovalley crafts deeply nourishing snacks and supplements made with organic ingredients and honorable sourcing. Wild Pastures connects small American farmers practicing regenerative agriculture with customers who believe better food is worth fighting for. Every product, every partnership, and every decision is guided by a commitment to real ingredients, regenerative practices, and the belief that health is built from the soil up.

We’re a team of grounded doers, curious thinkers, bold builders, and warm humans who like to laugh while doing meaningful work. We're growing quickly, fueled by purpose and a shared desire to repair the food system one thoughtful choice at a time. If you feel energized by impact, drawn to mission, and ready to join a company rewriting the future of food, we’d love to meet you!

Why This Role:

This is a defining opportunity to lead one of the most technically ambitious and capital-intensive transformations in physical logistics — building the automation and AI systems that will define how goods move through a $10B enterprise's distribution network for the next decade. The successful candidate will have the mandate, budget, and executive alignment to deploy Physical AI and robotics at scale across a national DC footprint.

• Own the Physical AI and robotics strategy for one of the largest logistics companies in North America

• Significant scope: full technology ownership across DC, warehouse, yard, cross-dock, and emerging automation platforms

• High-visibility executive role with direct line to C-suite and meaningful influence over major capital investment decisions

• Rare chance to sit at the frontier of OT/IT convergence — deploying computer vision, autonomous systems, and real-time intelligence in live fulfillment operations

• Competitive total compensation including base, annual bonus, and long-term incentive plan

Position Summary:

The Vice President of Technology – Distribution & Warehouse serves as the senior technology executive responsible for designing, building, and operating the full suite of technology platforms that power the company's distribution, warehousing, and supply chain fulfillment operations. This executive owns the technology roadmap across Distribution Centers (DCs), Warehouse Management, Yard Management, Cross-Dock Operations, and emerging Physical AI applications — directly enabling the speed, accuracy, and throughput of the company's physical logistics network.

This role sits at the intersection of technology and physical operations — partnering with DC GMs, operations leadership, and supply chain executives to deploy systems that drive measurable improvements in order accuracy, labor productivity, inventory precision, and dock-to-dock cycle times. VP will be a key voice in enterprise architecture, automation investment decisions, and the company's Physical AI and robotics strategy as it scales across a national network of facilities.

This position is based in our Penske Logistics development center in Beachwood, OH. This is an in-office position, at least 4 days a week. Relocation assistance may be available for qualified candidates.

Major Responsibilities:

Technology Strategy & Roadmap

• Define and own the multi-year technology roadmap for DC, warehouse, and yard management platforms, aligned to network growth, throughput targets, and the company's automation ambitions

• Lead the enterprise Physical AI strategy — evaluating AMR/AGV vendors, robotic picking systems, computer vision platforms, and AI-driven operational control systems for phased deployment across the DC network

• Drive build-vs-buy analysis and govern vendor selection for WMS, YMS, robotics, and automation investments at enterprise scale

• Serve as the technology voice in executive discussions on new DC openings

Position Overview

RAB is a fully remote, fully cloud-based company. We run a national lighting manufacturing and distribution business with no on-premises servers, no office network to babysit, and a modern SaaS stack already in place. The Director of Business Technology isn’t being hired to build that foundation — it’s built. We’re hiring someone to take it to the next level.

The next level is AI. We want a Director who sees every manual process, every handoff, and every report as a candidate for automation, and who is capable of actually doing it — evaluating tools, writing or directing the integrations, and shipping working systems that change how RAB operates. You’ll own IT strategy, cybersecurity, systems, and vendor relationships, and the environment has to stay secure and reliable — that’s table stakes.

The measure of success beyond that is how much of the business you’ve transformed.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is as comfortable in an API or a data pipeline as in a budget review, and who is excited that the tools now exist to rebuild how a mid-sized company works.

• 2-4 years of AI tools proficiency
• Demonstrated experience in IT infrastructure, desktop and server management, networking, cloud technologies, cybersecurity, vendor management, budgeting, and technology implementation.
• Experience with AWS/Azure and familiarity with programming or scripting languages.
• Experience with AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, or Git Hub Copilot preferred.
Core Competencies
• Technical Expertise – Strong knowledge of IT infrastructure, systems, and cloud technologies.
• Leadership and Team Development – Ability to lead, motivate, and develop IT personnel.

Posting Type

Hybrid/Remote

Job Overview

Relativity is looking for a Director to lead the systems team that manages and oversees the administration of key financial and business applications (e.g., Workday, Zuora, Adaptive, etc.) to make the finance organization successful. This position will play a critical part in the design and architecture of scalable finance systems to support the Company's financial data, business process, automation, and growth initiatives. As Relativity's cloud business scales, the role will ensure that usage-based billing, revenue recognition and financial reporting remain accurate, auditable, and highly automated. The role will report to the VP Accounting and work closely with IT, security, and other cross-functional teams. The role will also support the Company's international (multi-entity, multi-currency) operations, reporting and compliance.

Job Description and Requirements
• Own the design. delivery, and maintenance of financial systems and data including but not limited to: accounting, order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and budgeting platforms.
• Develop, implement and maintain policies and procedures for financial system operations, data management, and reporting.
• Oversee the accuracy and integrity of financial data in systems, ensuring compliance with relevant regulations and accounting standards.
• Optimize system functionality and drive tight integration across financial processes.
• Oversee system control environment and establish SOX compliant controls and frameworks
• Own IT general controls for in-scope financial systems (access management, change management, segregation of duties, vendor SOC reports) and partner with auditors, IT and security on control testing and remediation.
• Champion the accounting and finance organization's AI initiatives to help drive design, adoption and AI-managed tasks and projects, including leveraging native application functionality, Claude-driven processes and evaluation of other available AI platforms and technologies.
• Establish governance for AI use in finance workflows, including human review, data privacy, auditability and SOX control considerations.
• Support the flow of customer usage data from the RelativityaiR production environment through metering and rating to customer billing and revenue recognition (ASC 606), including usage reconciliation and data-quality controls.
• Maintain a multi-year financial systems roadmap, budget and vendor strategy, and support acquisition integration and new-entity setup.
• Partner with the IT business intelligence team to design, co-own and maintain the data lake for financial data to support advanced reporting needs and data integration.
• Stay updated on industry best practices and emerging technologies to recommend and implement innovative solutions.
• Collaborate with finance, revenue operations, procurement, global business operations and other teams to understand their needs and align financial systems with overall business

Purpose:

United Way of Northern New Jersey (UWNNJ) is seeking a strategic, innovative, collaborative, and results-oriented Senior Vice President, Technology to lead its enterprise technology, data, cybersecurity, AI, digital innovation, and business transformation strategy.

Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the SVP will ensure UWNNJ's technology and data capabilities are secure, scalable, integrated, and aligned with organizational priorities and mission impact. This position is hybrid.

UWNNJ is dedicated to improving the lives of ALICE® (Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed) households. Through United For ALICE, UWNNJ leverages research, data, partnerships, and innovation to deepen understanding of financial hardship and advance solutions that increase financial stability.

This is not a traditional IT leadership role. The SVP will connect technology directly to mission impact, fundraising, stakeholder engagement, operational effectiveness, and organizational growth. Working collaboratively across departments, the SVP will develop and execute a multi-year technology and business transformation roadmap that advances four strategic priorities:
• Understand ALICE:
Strengthen research, data, analytics, and actionable insights.
• Amplify ALICE:
Expand digital reach, communications, storytelling, and stakeholder engagement.
• Impact ALICE:
Advance fundraising, partnerships, programs, and data-informed solutions that improve financial stability.
• Equip the Organization:
Build the technology, cybersecurity, data, AI, infrastructure, and organizational capabilities needed to operate effectively and scale impact

Technology Strategy, Architecture & Governance

• Establish enterprise technology governance, investment priorities, performance measures, and accountability across departments and external partners
• Develop technology OKRs and report strategic progress, investments, opportunities, and risks to executive leadership and the Board
Enterprise Data Strategy & Governance
• Establish and lead an enterprise data strategy that strengthens data quality, accessibility, integration, stewardship, privacy, and analytics across UWNNJ and United For ALICE

Vizance is seeking a Director of Technology & Innovation to build, lead, and execute our technology strategy as we continue to grow. This is a new, hands-on position for someone who wants to learn the business, identify opportunities, and personally build the technology function Vizance needs for the future. This is an in-person position based in Vizance’s corporate office in Hartland, Wisconsin, where the individual will work closely with the executive team and leaders across the organization.

We are a growing independent insurance agency with approximately 320 associates across 25 locations in Wisconsin, Illinois, and Minnesota. Our growth strategy is built on three paths: organic growth, recruiting talented professionals, and mergers and acquisitions. Technology will play an important role in helping us scale each path while continuing to serve clients well and operate efficiently.

The right person will be excited to shape this new role, turn ideas into practical solutions, and build the technology capabilities Vizance needs for the future.

This role may be a strong fit for a technology leader, business analyst, business process analyst, systems leader, or operational technology professional who is ready to build, learn, and have a meaningful impact. CaptivateIQ is transforming the way companies plan, manage, and optimize sales performance.

We started with incentive compensation management and are now expanding our platform to solve broader enterprise performance management challenges. Recognized by analysts like Gartner, Forrester, and G2 and backed by investors including Sequoia, ICONIQ, Accel, and Sapphire Ventures, we help high-growth companies like Netflix, Figma, and Stripe drive revenue performance with flexibility and insight.
We’re building a category-defining platform at the intersection of finance, sales, operations, and AI. We’re looking for ambitious builders to help shape what comes next.
About the Role
As Senior Director of Engineering for Incentive Compensation Management (ICM), you’ll lead the engineering organization behind our flagship product that customers rely on to pay their teams accurately and motivate performance. You’ll lead managers across multiple teams and set the technical direction for making ICM AI-native without compromising the accuracy and trust our customers depend on.
This role combines product thinking, technical leadership, and organization building. You’ll partner closely with Product, Design, GTM, and executive leadership to turn ambiguous opportunities into scalable products, and you’ll shape the engineering culture and structure that delivers them.
 

The Problems You’ll Solve
-
Making ICM AI-native. Decide where AI creates real customer value in plan design, calculation, and payout workflows, and build the quality and evaluation practices that make those features trustworthy.

-
Scaling a system where correctness is non-negotiable. Customers pay real people based on our calculations. You’ll balance speed of delivery with reliability, performance, and data integrity at enterprise scale.

-
Evolving the organization with the product. You’ll develop managers, clarify ownership, and adapt structure and process as the product matures.
What You'll Do
Set the strategy

-
Own the engineering strategy for ICM, aligned with company priorities, customer needs, and long-term platform direction

-
Identify new opportunities and guide product evolution, including the thoughtful application of AI to create differentiated customer workflows

Lead the organization

-
Recruit, grow, and inspire engineering managers and senior technical leaders

-
Build a culture of ownership, velocity, and continuous improvement

-
Design team structures and processes that evolve with product maturity

Raise the technical bar

-
Guide architecture decisions that balance speed, scalability, reliability, and maintainability

-
Stay close enough to the work to spot risks, challenge assumptions, and raise quality across the organization. You don’t need to write production code, but you do need to earn the respect of the engineers who do.

Drive execution

-
Create alignment and clear priorities across Engineering, Product, Design, and GTM

-
Make thoughtful tradeoffs

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology on board 90% of the world's aircraft

Engines & Power Systems provides the propulsion, auxiliary power and electrical systems that keep those aircraft flying

Control Systems supplies the thermal and motion control systems that support takeoff, landing and the safety of everyone on board

Community Building & Coaching

As part of Supplier Assurance Services, you will assess the cybersecurity posture of third-party suppliers, influence risk decisions, and help strengthen the firm's global supply chain. oracle:marriott international:26146916.description:
JOB SUMMARY

Provides a high level of property maintenance knowledge. Position has overall responsibility for maintaining the building, grounds and physical plant with particular attention towards safety, security and asset protection. Accountable for managing the budget, capital expenditure projects, preventative maintenance and energy conservation. Develops and implements strategies that will deliver products and services, which meet or exceed the needs and expectations of guests and employees while maximizing the financial performance. Responsible for maintaining standards and regulatory requirements. Leads the emergency response team for all facility issues.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or GED; 6 years experience in the engineering and maintenance or related professional area; technical training in HVAC-R/Electrical/Plumbing.

OR

• 2-year degree from an accredited university in Building and Construction, Engineering, Mechanics, or related major; 4 years experience in the engineering and maintenance or related professional area; technical training in HVAC-R/Electrical/Plumbing.

CORE WORK ACTIVITIES

Managing Engineering Operations and Budgets

• Works with property and regional engineering leadership team to determine how Engineering is performing against budget and highlights areas of concern to leadership.

• Manages the physical plant including equipment, refrigeration, HVAC, plumbing, water treatment and electrical systems in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures.

• Administers service contracts to support property needs.

• Ensures fire crew has complete understanding of all procedures, equipment and alarms.

• Coaches and supports engineering leadership team to effectively manage controllable expenses (e.g., wages, heat, light and power, water consumption, tools and equipment, grounds keeping supplies, uniforms, vendors, service agreements, inventory, etc.).

• Manages and controls heat, light and power.

• Develops an engineering operating strategy that is aligned with the property/brand’s business strategy.

• Develops and manages Engineering budget.

• Ensures integration of departmental goals in game plans.

• Oversees execution of long term preventative maintenance and 10 year asset protection plans.

• Reviews financial reports and statements to determine how Engineering is performing against budget.

• Addresses potential areas of concern and proposing solutions to owners in a proactive manner.

• Communicates a clear and consistent message regarding departmental goals to produce desired results.

• Supervises construction to ensure timely completion of projects within budgetary guidelines.

Maintaining Engineering Standards

• Ensures compliance with state, local and federal regulations.

• Maintains property life safety systems (e.g., fire fighting equipment, sprinkler systems, and alarm systems).

• Ensures building and equipment licenses, permits and certifications are current.

JOB SUMMARY

Manages security/loss prevention operations on a daily basis. Areas of responsibilities include protection of property assets, employees, guests and property, accident and fire prevention and response. Ensures that all areas of the property are safe and secure. Maintains logs, certifications and documents required by law and Standard Operating Procedures. Strives to continually improve guest and employee satisfaction while maximizing the financial performance of the department.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or GED; 4 years experience in the security/loss prevention or related professional area.

OR

• 2-year degree from an accredited university in Criminal Justice or related major; 2 years experience in the security/loss prevention or related professional area.

CORE WORK ACTIVITIES

Managing Security/Loss Prevention Operations

• Assists in the development and implementation of emergency procedures.

• Conducts investigation of all losses of property assets and refers to proper management for disposition.

• Deploys security staff to effectively monitor and protect property assets.

• Comply with all Corporate Loss Prevention safety and security management guidelines and procedures.

• Conduct periodic patrols of entire property and parking areas.

• Recognize success across areas of responsibility.

• Handles complaints, settling disputes, and resolving grievances and conflicts, or otherwise negotiating with others.

• Identifies and makes recommendations for minimizing physical hazards and unsafe work practices.

• Implements action plans to monitor and control risk.

• Maintains required reports and documentation regarding patrols of property and parking areas.

• Provides means for obtaining necessary medical attention on a timely basis.

Leading Security/Loss Prevention Teams

• Attends pre- and post-convention and weekly forecast meetings to understand group needs and gather critical information to communicate to Loss Prevention officers.

• Celebrates successes by publicly recognizing the contributions of team members.

• Communicates the importance of safety procedures, detailing procedure codes, ensuring employee understanding of safety codes, monitoring processes and procedures related to safety.

• Encourages and builds mutual trust, respect, and cooperation among team members.

oracle:mattson technology:3208.description:
About Mattson

Company: Mattson Technology, Inc., a 38-year Silicon Valley company, designs, manufactures, markets, and globally supports plasma and rapid thermal processing equipment to fabricate integrated circuits for the global semiconductor industry.

Mattson Technology, Inc. offers processing equipment that utilizes innovative technologies to deliver advanced processing capabilities and high productivity for the fabrication of current and next-generation integrated circuits. Our equipment and technologies are used by leading memory and logic, analog /power device manufacturers worldwide. sitemap:at&t:103492691056.description:
This is a full-time onsite role based in the location(s) posted and is performed from the designated work location five days per week. No relocation is offered.

AT&T will not hire any applicants for this position who require employer sponsorship now or in the future.

Join AT&T and reimagine the communications and technologies that connect the world. The Technology Services organization is responsible for advancing information technology performance and delivering solutions with a focus on maximizing ROI, increasing efficiency and enhancing the experience of end users. Guided by experienced leaders, Corporate Systems seamlessly integrate with advanced Technology and Operations to drive our enterprise forward. Our Systems Reliability and Software Delivery teams are unwavering in their commitment to excellence, ensuring every solution is robust and efficient. When you step into a career with AT&T, you won't just imagine the future, you'll create it.

What You'll Do

The Director sets and governs AT&T's target-state architecture across the Consumer, Business and Corporate IT domains. The role owns the enterprise taxonomy, the technology standards and the architecture decision rights that turn business strategy into rationalized, reliable and AI-enabled technology portfolios. The Director leads through others at scale, builds coalitions with peer Directors and AVPs, and makes strategic, market-informed trade-offs.

Target State and Strategy
- Define and maintain target-state and transition-state architectures, domain roadmaps and integrated product roadmaps that align with business strategy and value streams.
- Make the traceability chain work in practice: customer journey → business capability → business process → functional capability → IT application.
- Drive portfolio rationalization, using lifecycle disposition (invest, sustain, migrate, retire) and TCO as the financial lens.

Domain Architecture and Taxonomy
- Own the EA taxonomy, the application classification model and the business capability maps, and keep them as the authoritative system of record.
- Lead domain architects across Mass Markets, ABS and Corporate Systems domains. Organize the work around domain clusters and domain-specific platforms.
- Make sure taxonomy data in tools like ServiceNow APM, LeanIX and other EA repositories is accurate, governed and usable in decisions.

Technology Standards and Lifecycle
- Establish and enforce enterprise technology standards, reference architectures, patterns and certified enterprise services.
- Run technology lifecycle management: emerging, standard, contain, sunset and retire.
- Promote reuse of components, services and patterns to reduce complexity and cost.

Decision Rights and Governance
- Define and operate the architecture decision-rights model: who decides, who is consulted and how decisions get escalated, across the enterprise, domain and solution tiers.
- Chair or co-chair the Architecture Review Board and the standards councils. Ow

sitemap:citi (jobs.citi.com):10281064267.description:
Markets Operations Process Engineering drives transformational change across the organization's processes, controls and architecture. We partner closely with our Operations and Technology teams to build strategy and deliver a multi-year transformation, overseeing the execution with formal program management and portfolio management methodologies will leveraging data and new capabilities such as AI to optimize outcomes and business decision making. Our goal is to deliver best-in-class transformation to enable our Operations professionals to excel with client service excellence, robust risk management and continuous improvement. This role pertains to Payments transformation.
The Program Management Senior Lead is a strategic professional who closely follows latest trends in own field and adapts them for application within own job and the business. Typically a small number of people within the business that provide the same level of expertise. Excellent communication skills required in order to negotiate internally, often at a senior level. Developed communication and diplomacy skills are required in order to guide, influence and convince others, in particular colleagues in other areas and occasional external customers. Accountable for significant direct business results or authoritative advice regarding the operations of the business. Necessitates a degree of responsibility over technical strategy. Primarily affects a sub-function. Responsible for handling staff management issues, including resource management and allocation of work within the team/project.

Responsibilities:

About Citi:
Citi, the leading global bank, has approximately 200 million customer accounts and does business in more than 160 countries and jurisdictions. Citi provides consumers, corporations, governments, and institutions with a broad range of financial products and services, including consumer banking and credit, corporate and investment banking, securities brokerage, transaction services, and wealth management.

As a bank with a brain and a soul, Citi creates economic value that is systemically responsible and in our clients' best interests. As a financial institution that touches every region of the world and every sector that shapes your daily life, our Enterprise Operations & Technology teams are charged with a mission that rivals any large tech company. Our technology solutions are the foundations of everything we do from keeping the bank safe, managing global resources, and providing the technical tools our workers need to be successful to designing our digital architecture and ensuring our platforms provide a first-class customer experience. We reimagine client and partner experiences to deliver excellence through secure, reliable, and efficient services.

Our commitment to diversity includes a workforce that represents the clients we serve from all walks of life, backgrounds, and origins. We foster an environment where the best people want to work. We value and demand respect for others, promote individuals based on merit, and ensure opportunities for personal development are widely available to all. Ideal candidates are innovators with well-rounded backgrounds who bring their authentic selves to work and complement our culture of delivering results with pride. If you are a problem solver who seeks passion in your work, come join us. We'll enable growth and progress together.

About the Team:
The Data Governance and Controls Lead is a strategic professional at the heart of Citi's enterprise-wide data integrity mission. This role sits at the intersection of risk, policy, and data — shaping the frameworks that govern how one of the world's most complex financial institutions identifies, measures, and manages data as a critical asset. Becoming a City employee means being a part of a team that cares about making a difference. Your work will shape both the present and future of San Francisco. When you work for the City, you’re choosing a job with purpose.
The Mission of the San Francisco Department of Public Health (SFDPH) is to protect and promote the health of all San Franciscans. Fulfilling this mission requires employees working across our hospitals, clinics, programs, and offices to deliver services and support the communities we serve. Individuals interested in joining SFDPH should expect to work in person across these settings.
The San Francisco Health Network, Population Health, Behavioral Health Services, and Administration are the core divisions of SFDPH. The San Francisco Health Network is the City’s only complete system of care and has locations throughout the City, including Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital and Trauma Center, Laguna Honda Hospital and Rehabilitation Center, and over 15 primary care health centers. The Population Health Division (PHD) provides core public health services for the City and County of San Francisco: health protection, health promotion, disease and injury prevention, and disaster preparedness and response. Behavioral Health Services operates in conjunction with SFHN and provides a range of mental health and substance use treatment services.

smartrecruiters:harvard university:37439.description:
By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.
Why join the Harvard Radcliffe Institute?
The Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University, known colloquially as Harvard Radcliffe Institute, is one of the world’s leading centers for interdisciplinary exploration. We bring together students, scholars, artists, and practitioners to pursue curiosity-driven research, expand human understanding, and grapple with questions that demand insight from across disciplines.
The Fellowship Program annually supports the work of 50 leading artists and scholars. Academic Ventures fosters collaborative research projects and sponsors lectures and conferences that engage scholars with the public. The Schlesinger Library documents the lives of American women of the past and present for the future, furthering the Institute's commitment to women, gender, and society. The Emerging Leaders Program is a youth leadership development program partnering local high school sophomores with Harvard undergraduates in a mentoring relationship.
The Institute’s work is shaped by its history as the former Radcliffe College—a school founded to ensure that the standard of education embodied in Harvard was accessible to women, who were then excluded from the University. But the legacy of Radcliffe College is not simply coeducation at Harvard; it is the recognition that universities will always be greater when they draw wisdom and talent from the widest possible pool.
Take a look at this video to get different staff perspectives on working at Harvard Radcliffe Institute !

Why join the Harvard Radcliffe Institute?
The Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University, known colloquially as Harvard Radcliffe Institute, is one of the world’s leading centers for interdisciplinary exploration. We bring together students, scholars, artists, and practitioners to pursue curiosity-driven research, expand human understanding, and grapple with questions that demand insight from across disciplines.
The Fellowship Program annually supports the work of 50 leading artists and scholars. Academic Ventures fosters collaborative research projects and sponsors lectures and conferences that engage scholars with the public. The Schlesinger Library documents the lives of American women of the past and present for the future, furthering the Institute's commitment to women, gender, and society. The Emerging Leaders Program is a youth leadership development program partnering local high school sophomores with Harvard undergraduates in a mentoring relationship.
The Institute’s work is shaped by its history as the former Radcliffe College—a school founded to ensure that the standard of education embodied in Harvard was accessible to women, who were then excluded from the University. But the legacy of Radcliffe College is not simply coeducation at Harvard; it is the recognition that universities will always be greater when they draw wisdom and talent from the widest possible pool.

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description
The Director, Third-Party Cyber Defense is Allstate’s senior leader for supplier cyber incident response. The role is accountable for how quickly and appropriately Allstate understands and responds when a supplier is compromised. This leader sets direction for two functions: Supplier Incident Investigation & Response, and Supplier Monitoring & Intelligence. The Director also owns the technical inventory of supplier connections and leads targeted technical assessments when incidents, intelligence, or monitoring signals call for a closer look.

The role calls for an experienced incident response leader who understands how suppliers connect to large enterprises and can build a team that performs consistently under pressure. As a member of the Cyber Defense & Response leadership team, the Director partners with Enterprise TPRM, Procurement, Legal & Privacy, and Security Operations. Together they deliver fast, fact-based answers about Allstate’s exposure and a stronger supplier ecosystem after every event.

As a Director, you won’t just deliver results – you drive our culture and shared purpose. You can work remotely and will commute to a nearby office and/or travel for meaningful connection opportunities.

A supplier just told us they’ve been breached.
It is now one of the most common ways a cyber incident reaches a large company: a claims vendor, a payroll provider, a SaaS platform, a file-transfer service. The notice is usually short and vague. From that moment, five questions decide whether Allstate handles it well:
- Do they have our data? Which data, about which customers, in which states.
- How do they reach us? Every network link, API, file transfer, and service account, and whether we can shut each one down safely.
- What did we already know about them? Their risk tier, their last assessment, and the findings that are still open.
- What do they owe us? The notification, cooperation, and audit terms in their contract, and whether they are living up to them.
- What is the right response? Action that fits the facts: enough to protect our customers, without shutting down a business process when the facts don’t call for it.

The best third-party programs answer all five within hours, every time. Not because someone heroic stays up all night, but because the assessments were done, the connections were mapped, the playbook was practiced, and the working relationships with Legal, Privacy, Procurement, and Security Operations were in place before the call came.

Job Description
SUMMARY
Ares Management is seeking a highly motivated Vice President, AI Platform Engineering to help design, build, and scale the firm's enterprise AI platform and the production-grade capabilities that support AI solutions across the organization.

This is a senior, highly hands-on engineering role within the central Data & AI organization. The VP will have significant ownership of the core AI platform , including the common services, infrastructure, and developer capabilities used by AI applications, agents, and technology teams across the firm.

The successful candidate will combine strong software and platform engineering fundamentals with practical experience building Generative AI and machine learning systems in production. They will own major platform components and technical workstreams, contribute to platform architecture and engineering standards, and build reusable services that allow teams across Ares to develop AI applications securely, reliably, and at scale.

The role will work closely with AI Engineering leadership, Data Engineering, AI Product Management, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Architecture, and business-aligned technology teams. This individual will also serve as a senior technical partner to engineers adopting shared AI platform capabilities.

REPORTING RELATION S
Reports to: Principal, Head of AI Platform & Engineering
Supervises: Individual contributors and/or technical workstreams as required

PRIMARY FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBILITIES
Core AI Platform Engineering
- Design, build, and operate production-grade services that form the foundation of Ares' enterprise AI platform.
- Own major platform components and technical workstreams from architecture and design through implementation, deployment, and ongoing operation.

Associate/Vice President, Investment Data Management (PFS)

Company Description
HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock, is a leading global, credit-focused alternative investment manager that seeks to provide creative capital solutions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our clients. We manage various strategies across the capital structure, including privately negotiated senior debt; privately negotiated junior capital solutions in debt, preferred and equity formats; liquid credit including syndicated leveraged loans, collateralized loan obligations and high yield bonds; asset-based finance and real estate. The scale and breadth of our platform offers the flexibility to invest in companies large and small, through standard or customized solutions. At our core, we share a common thread of intellectual rigor and discipline that enables us to create value for our clients.

HPS was established in 2007 as a unit of Highbridge Capital Management, LLC (“HCM”), a subsidiary of JPMorgan Asset Management (“JPMAM”). On March 31, 2016, the senior executives of HPS acquired HPS and its subsidiaries from JPMAM and HCM (the “Transaction”. Following the Transaction, JPMAM retained a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently redeemed in April 2022. In June 2018, affiliates of Dyal Capital Partners made a passive minority investment in HPS. In February 2022, an affiliate of The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America made a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently increased in August 2024. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock acquired the business and assets of HPS, with 100% of consideration paid in BlackRock equity (the “HPS/BlackRock Transaction”).

The HPS/BlackRock Transaction brings together BlackRock’s corporate and asset owner relationships with HPS’s diversified origination and capital flexibility. BlackRock and HPS have formed a new private financing solutions business unit (“PFS”) led by Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson, creating an integrated franchise with approximately $370 billion in client assets, including $205 billion of private credit assets. This combined platform, which has more than 590 investment professionals and approximately 1,300 employees globally, offers broad capabilities across senior and junior credit solutions, asset-based finance, real estate, CLOs and GP-LP solutions. As part of the HPS/BlackRock Transaction, Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson have joined BlackRock’s Global Executive Committee, and Scott Kapnick has been appointed as an observer to the BlackRock Board.

About this role

The Aladdin Platform Engineering – Engineering Services team builds the platforms, pipelines, and developer tooling that thousands of engineers across BlackRock use every day to design, build, and ship software. Security is engineered into that path rather than inspected at the end of it: the same teams that own build systems, artifact repositories, and deployment pipelines also own the guardrails, evidence, and automated controls that make secure delivery the default.

You will lead the cybersecurity engineering function inside this group, working alongside platform engineering, product management, risk, and the firm’s information security organization to protect a large, cloud-native, AI-enabled, highly regulated financial services firm.

Your role and impact

As Director for Cybersecurity Engineering, you’ll set the technical strategy for how security is built into software delivery and cloud infrastructure at scale. Software supply chain integrity is your first principle: every artifact the firm ships should carry verifiable provenance, and every release should be attested — signed, traceable to its source and build environment, and admissible as evidence without anyone assembling it after the fact. You’ll lead BlackRock toward that future state, moving the organization from periodic inspection of what was built to continuous, cryptographic proof of how it was built, with trust decisions made against attestations rather than assumptions.

You’ll treat DevSecOps as the operating principle that makes this achievable — policy as code, automated enforcement in continuous integration and delivery pipelines, and time-boxed exceptions with audit-ready evidence generated automatically. You’ll extend that same provenance and trust model to AI-assisted development and agentic workflows, where model-generated code, prompt injection, and non-human identities create new classes of exposure and demand policy-driven defense in depth.

Your responsibilities

No matter your role at BlackRock, you’ll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, stay curious and adaptable as the business evolves, and take end-to-end ownership of outcomes that matter to clients. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities:
- Own the software supply chain security strategy end to end — source integrity, dependency and artifact provenance, software bills of materials, signing, and verifiable build attestation across the firm’s technology estate
- Secure the build and release path itself, hardening build systems, artifact repositories, and deployment pipelines as high-value targets, and enforcing trust decisions at admission based on attested provenance rather than implicit trust
