Your team

BlackRock is seeking a Director to lead data stewardship for the Assets & Opportunity data domains within the BlackRock Data Office (BDO), reporting directly to the Global Head of Data Stewardship for the BDO.

The BDO, part of Aladdin Data, accelerates how data is onboarded, governed, managed and consumed through the firm’s Enterprise Data Platform, so that trusted, reusable and AI-ready data can be managed as a strategic enterprise asset supporting operational excellence, analytics, AI innovation, and our 2030 strategy.

Your role and impact

As the domain data steward for the Assets & Opportunity pillar, the Director will stand up and manage a centralized stewardship function to deliver a trusted client-level and business-specific view of assets under management (AUM) and net new assets to the global enterprise, working closely with Client Business COOs, the Global Product Solutions organization, and Finance.

The Director will also define and drive the Walletshare data strategy (the share of a client’s total assets that BlackRock manages versus competitors), unifying the full “addressable wallet” view of the client to enable our client businesses’ growth goals.

- Governance & Process Centralization : Oversee data governance for AUM & Flows and Walletshare as the accountable steward for business definitions, critical data elements, data quality rules and decision rights. At Cadence, we hire and develop leaders and innovators who want to make an impact on the world of technology.
Cadence Solutions (North America) team is looking for an experienced candidate to lead Front End Design projects. This is a challenging and rewarding opportunity is for a highly motivated engineer with a passion for innovation and a proven track record of success in the semiconductor industry.
This is a leadership role where you will be responsible for:
Technical Leadership:
Guide and mentor a team of RTL design engineers, fostering a collaborative and innovative environment.
Design & Microarchitecture:
Define and develop microarchitectural features for IPs and subsystems, ensuring they meet PPA goals.
RTL Development:
Write, debug, and optimize RTL code in Verilog, SystemVerilog, or VHDL to create complex digital logic.
Verification & Signoff:
Oversee pre-silicon verification activities, including Lint, Clock Domain Crossing (CDC), Formal Verification (FV), and other quality checks.
Collaboration:
Work closely with cross-functional teams, including Design Verification (DV), Physical Design (PD), Architecture, and firmware engineers, to ensure successful delivery.
Qualifications:
*10+ years of Front End design and/or verification with a BS/MS Engineering or Computer Sciences
*Proven experience in leading and managing complex engineering projects
*Rich experience in IP creation and/or SoC and IP (CPU, Memory, Interface) integration
*Expert in RTL design (Verilog), simulators debuggers
*Hands on Experience in Synthesis, SDC creation and support PD and STA teams.
*Experience in driving results in multi-disciplinary organization
Desirable:
A Self-motivated person with good communication and design management skills
Experience with Cadence front end toolset

workday:calistacorp:Yulista Services LLC.description:
Yulista Services LLC

Regular

Job Summary
Yulista’s Mission Support & Training (MS&T) business line is seeking a Director of Engineering Programs to provide leadership and oversight of engineering programs supporting the Department of War (DoW), NASA, and other federal customers.

Based at the corporate headquarters in Huntsville, Alabama, this position is responsible for the successful execution, financial performance, strategic growth, and operational integration of current and future engineering programs. The Director reports to the Senior Vice President of MS&T and partners closely with executive leadership, engineering, business development, finance, contracts, and customers to drive operational excellence, business growth, and exceptional customer satisfaction.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
- Provide active leadership and oversight of Yulista's engineering program portfolio.
- Maintain full program management responsibility, including revenue, profitability, forecasting, budgeting, and overall financial performance.
- Partner with the Chief Engineer and organic engineering team to ensure successful execution of program cost, schedule, technical, quality, and customer objectives.
- Lead program execution across multiple contracts, ensuring effective risk management, resource allocation, and operational performance.
- Collaborate with Business Development and Capture teams to support strategic growth initiatives, proposal development, pricing, contract transitions, and customer pursuits.
- Build and maintain strong executive-level customer relationships while ensuring high levels of customer satisfaction.
- Work with the organic engineering managers to align workforce planning, staffing, technical capabilities, and resource management with program requirements.
- Ensure compliance with contractual requirements, regulatory standards, quality systems, and corporate policies.
- Develop and implement standardized program management processes while fostering a culture of continuous improvement.
- Mentor engineering team and support the development of future technical leadership.
- Support strategic planning efforts and the continued growth and expansion of the organization's engineering capabilities.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline.
- Minimum of 15 years of progressively responsible experience managing complex engineering, aerospace, aviation, or DoW programs.
- Minimum of 7 years of leadership experience managing multiple programs, portfolios, or technical organizations.
- Demonstrated success managing program budgets, forecasting, financial reporting, contract performance, and overall program execution.
- Experience managing government contracts, customer relationships, subcontractors, and cross-functional teams.
- Experience supporting business development, capture efforts, proposal development, and program transitions.
- Excellent leaders

Callaway Golf Company is a premium golf equipment, gear and apparel company with a portfolio of global brands, including Callaway Golf, Odyssey, TravisMathew, and OGIO. Director, Data Scientist - Global Payment Network

Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

workday:capital one:R1005541.description:
Director, Tech Risk & Analysis

Do you love navigating complex technology landscapes and safeguarding critical systems? Do you enjoy solving complex business problems in a fast-paced, collaborative, inclusive, and risk-conscious delivery environment? At Capital One, you'll be part of a big group of makers, breakers, doers and disruptors who love to solve real problems and meet real customer needs. We are seeking Tech Risk & Analysis Professionals who are passionate about cyber best practices, threat analysis, and risk mitigation to join our team. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to be on the forefront of driving cybersecurity governance, resilience, and risk transformation across Capital One.

Summary:
- Applies expertise on cyber best practices to assess current state, identify gaps, and assess cyber risk, threats, and business impact
- Cybersecurity area-specific SME [knowledge of risk frameworks, information security risk assessments, information risk controls, regulatory and internal governance], data analysis [metrics and reporting], and customer engagement
- Acts as a master storyteller and strategic translator, bridging the gap between technical cybersecurity experts and executive leadership by synthesizing complex risk data into clear, compelling narratives.
- Drives the overarching strategy, framework, and execution of executive and Board-level reporting, ensuring alignment across the enterprise's cyber risk posture and strategic imperatives.

Responsibilities:
- Leads the Cyber Strategy & Reporting team in designing, structuring, and producing executive- and Board-level reporting materials—including quarterly risk updates, strategic briefings, and committee read-outs—for the CISO and senior leadership.

Job Description:
About the Role
The Director, Product Engineering will lead the team responsible for our care management applications and the vendor integrations that connect them to the rest of the care ecosystem, including EHRs, scheduling systems, and other external health systems. The Director will manage a team of engineering managers and senior engineers, while serving as a hands-on technical leader who sets the standard through their own contributions to the code.
This role sits at the center of our next phase of AI transformation. We’ve embraced AI to empower our engineers, using Cursor and agentic tooling for triage, automated updates, and faster feature delivery. Now we’re moving toward fully agentic development, where AI agents take work from ticket through product requirements, engineering design, and implementation within well-defined guardrails. The Director will define the strategy, priorities, validation, and review practices that make this possible, shifting our product engineers from building individual features to designing the systems and guardrails that let agents do that work safely and reliably.
The Director will partner closely with product, design, clinical operations, data science, and data platform teams to deliver technology that drives tech-enabled care for underserved populations. We’re looking for a leader who is equally comfortable growing people and writing code, and who is deeply curious about, and energized by, what AI-first engineering makes possible.

Responsibilities
- Lead and mentor a team of engineering managers and senior technical leaders, setting clear, measurable goals and building a strong bench of future leaders
- Own the strategy, roadmap, and long-term health of our care management applications and the vendor integrations that connect to them (EHR, scheduling, and other external systems)
- Define and drive our path to fully agentic development workflows, where agents move work from ticket to product requirements doc, to engineering design doc, to shipped code
- Design and maintain the guardrails, validation processes, and review personas that allow agents to safely run the full development lifecycle
- Shift the team’s focus from hand-building features to designing, evaluating, and improving the agentic systems that build them
- Evaluate and adopt AI and agent tooling (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, Mastra, and similar agent frameworks) and establish best practices across the organization
- Remain a hands-on contributor, writing and reviewing well-tested, scalable code to maintain technical credibility and unblock critical initiatives
- Partner with Product, Design, Clinical Operations, Data Platform, and Analytics to gather requirements, align priorities, and deliver complete capabilities
- Influence architectural and technology decisions across engineering and adjacent functions, and resolve cross-team conflicts and escalations
- Communicate technical strategy clearly to both technical and non-technic

Collectors is the leading creator of innovative technology that provides value-added services for collectors worldwide. We grade, authenticate, vault, and sell millions of record-setting collectibles, all while modernizing and digitalizing the process to further our mission of helping collectors pursue their passions. We’re always on the lookout for talented people to join our growing team.

Our services span collectible trading cards, autographs, comic books, coins, video games, event tickets, and memorabilia. Our subsidiaries include PSA, PCGS, Beckett, SGC, and Card Ladder.

Since our founding in 1986, we have graded and authenticated millions of items. We employ more than 3000 people across our headquarters in Santa Ana, California and offices in New Jersey, Texas, Florida, Japan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canada, Mexico, Germany, and France.

As part of our interview process, we request that candidates have their cameras on during video interviews. This helps foster meaningful conversation and allows us to create an experience that closely resembles our standard working environment. Certain interview steps may take place by phone. For remote roles, and at our discretion, candidates may be asked to participate in an on-site interview as part of the final stages of the process.

About the Cornell Lab of Ornithology

The Cornell Lab of Ornithology is the world's leading resource for conservation, research, education, and participatory science focused on birds and biodiversity. The Lab is a vibrant unit within Cornell's College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS), where twelve world-class, mission-driven programs are directed by full-time faculty and other renowned professionals. Lab staff teach undergraduate courses, advise graduate students, collect and disseminate world-famous digital resources on biodiversity, and engage with partner organizations and public citizens around the world to conduct scientific enterprises and conservation action. Our management and staff are committed to the highest standards of ethics and excellence in all areas of our work, and our Board leadership includes faculty from Cornell and other universities, successful entrepreneurs and managers from the business and non-profit sectors, and conservation-minded citizens from the United States and beyond.

The Lab’s Innovation & Integrated Technology Office (LiiT) provides strategic technology leadership to advance the Cornell Lab of Ornithology’s mission. Working across centers and in partnership with Cornell University and external collaborators, LiiT connects technology investments, platforms, data, and services to the Lab’s goals in biodiversity science, public engagement, training, conservation action, and workplace collaboration.

LiiT’s IT Innovation Roadmap is organized around five interconnected pillars: Enterprise Data, Cloud & AI; Digital Engagement & Next-Generation Experiences; Customer Service & Experience Excellence; Digital Convening & Partner Networks; and Operational Excellence & Resilience. Together, these pillars guide the development of shared capabilities that support the Lab’s programs, strengthen global partnerships, and translate scientific knowledge into conservation impact.

Guided by the themes of ONE Lab, SCALE, and RESILIENT, LiiT advances cross-center collaboration, coordinated program delivery, responsible adoption of AI, and reliable, secure technology operations. Its work brings strategic planning and implementation together through clear priorities, effective governance, resource coordination, and measurable outcomes.

Job Description Summary
Cushman & Wakefield is hiring a Director of Advisory Architecture to lead architecture for its advisory business, improve the tools and processes that speed up development, and champion forward deployed engineering (FDE). Job Description
Cushman & Wakefield is hiring a Director of Advisory Architecture to lead architecture for its advisory business, improve the tools and processes that speed up development, and champion forward deployed engineering (FDE). The Director is an architect first, and the role has three parts: sound architecture for advisory solutions, ongoing optimization of development tools and processes (including accelerators such as AI Studio), and championing the FDE model of embedded, prototype-first delivery.
The role combines deep solution and cloud architecture, including platforms such as Salesforce, with hands-on experience in agentic architecting and rapid, embedded development. The goal is for fast prototypes and AI-assisted work to be promoted into production by Engineering without rework, and for the architecture behind them to hold up.
The Director reports to the Head of Architecture and partners closely with Product, Business Analysis, Solution Architecture, and Engineering. Our customers are internal: brokers, other employees, and contractors who need technology that fits how they work.

What you will do
- Own architecture for the advisory business. Set the target architecture, standards, and roadmap for advisory solutions, and make sure designs are sound, secure, and consistent with company architecture standards.
- Optimize tools and processes. Continuously improve the tools, templates, and ways of working that shorten the development lifecycle from idea to production, including accelerators such as AI Studio.
- Practice agentic architecting. Define how AI agents are used to draft requirements, design solutions, and generate code, with human review, clear patterns, and quality controls at each step.
- Champion FDE. Lead and grow an embedded team that works with brokers and delivery teams to build working solutions quickly, iterate live on feedback, and decide with the business sponsor whether each effort is productized, handed off, or retired.
- Protect the path to production. Work with peer architecture leaders and Engineering on the guardrails prototypes are built within, a promotion gate to production, and shared source control, environments, and standards.
- Triage with Product. Agree on criteria for which requests enter the FDE lane and which follow the standard requirements, design, and build path, and cap FDE capacity so it does not become a help desk.

We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Position Summary

The Lead Director - Security Operations Center (SOC) is responsible for leading the cybersecurity operations function for a rapidly evolving healthcare business, ensuring the organization can effectively detect, investigate, respond to, and recover from cybersecurity threats.  By establishing strong operational processes, actionable threat intelligence, and effective response capabilities, the position helps protect critical business operations, sensitive data, and customer trust.

As the leader of the SOC function, this role is accountable for building and maturing security operations capabilities that balance security, scalability, and business agility. The Lead Director partners closely with infrastructure, cloud, identity, engineering, and business leaders to strengthen cyber resilience and prepare the organization for emerging threats. Through strong leadership, operational discipline, and continuous improvement, this position helps ensure cybersecurity remains an enabler of growth while reducing risk in a highly regulated environment.

Key Responsibilities:

Security Operations Leadership
- Lead the strategy, execution, and continuous improvement of the Security Operations Center, including threat monitoring, detection, investigation, response, and threat hunting activities.
- Establish operational processes, service levels, metrics, and reporting to measure effectiveness and support informed decision-making.
- Build and mature SOC capabilities that align security operations to business priorities, risk tolerance, and growth objectives.
- Ensure operational readiness, escalation procedures, and effective coordination during cybersecurity events and incidents.

Threat Detection & Incident Response
- Serve as the primary escalation point for significant cyber incidents and coordinate response efforts across technical and business stakeholders.
- Drive improvements in detection engineering, investigation processes, and response workflows to reduce risk and improve response times.

Location – Remote, commutable to London office as and when required
Type – Permanent, Full-time 37.5 hours

Velonetic helps keep the London insurance market moving. With more than 100 years of market heritage, we combine specialist insurance expertise, proven processes and technology to make complex insurance operations simpler, faster and more reliable.

- Knowledge of modern data platforms, analytics and AI-readiness.
- Strong understanding of data risk, privacy and regulatory requirements.
- Ideally, experience within insurance, financial services or another highly regulated industry.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB
The Director, Digital, Data & AI owns and operates Ebara Elliott Energy's (EEE) Digital Program end-to-end. This role brings the Automation & AI team, data engineering, data science and analytics, and application development together under one accountable leader to instill day-to-day program discipline, including prioritization, value tracking, fail-fast decision-making, and Finance-facing case-building. The role involves assessing the internal team to remove duplicative work and deliberately building toward a variable-cost model that incorporates offshore delivery capacity, managed services, and close partnership with EEE’s incoming IT Shared Services organization. As a senior engineering leader at Generac, you will lead a team of systems engineers who own the end-to-end architecture, integration, and validation of industrial diesel and gaseous-fueled generator sets. You will make sure that the engine, alternator, controls, cooling, fuel, exhaust/aftertreatment, and enclosure subsystems work together as one reliable, certifiable, and cost-competitive product. What You'll Do
- Own the system architecture for industrial diesel and gas generator sets, including the integration of the engine, alternator, excitation/AVR, governor, controller, cooling, fuel, exhaust/aftertreatment, and enclosure subsystems.

- Define and govern system interfaces with internal teams and with engine, alternator, and controls suppliers.
- Direct system verification and validation, including transient/load acceptance, derating, sound, vibration, emissions, and certification testing to UL 2200, NFPA 110, and ISO 8528.

- Lead system risk management (SFMEA/DFMEA, fault tree analysis, DVP&R) and technical trade studies to meet reliability, cost, and performance targets.
- Own technical design reviews and engineering gate criteria within the stage-gate product development process.
- Champion model-based systems engineering (MBSE) and simulation to reduce test iterations and time to market.
- Partner with Quality, Service, and Applications Engineering on field failure root cause analysis (8D, fishbone) and feed lessons learned into design standards.
- Build, coach, and develop a high-performing systems engineering team, including recruiting, retention, and succession planning.

Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering or a related field.
- 12+ years of engineering experience (15+ years for Sr. Director), including 10+ years in the design, integration, or validation of generator sets, reciprocating engines, or comparable heavy-duty power systems.
- Director: 5+ years leading systems or multidisciplinary engineering teams.
- Hands-on experience with systems engineering practices: requirements management, interface control, DFMEA/SFMEA, DVP&R, and stage-gate design reviews.
- Working knowledge of UL 2200, NFPA 110, NFPA 70 (NEC), ISO 8528, and EPA emissions requirements.

Georgetown University comprises two unique campuses in the nation’s capital. With the Hilltop Campus located in the heart of the historic Georgetown neighborhood, and the Capitol Campus, just minutes from the U.S. Capitol and U.S. Supreme Court, Georgetown University offers rigorous academic programs, a global perspective, and unparalleled opportunities to engage with Washington, D.C. Requirements

Job Overview

The Institute for Technology Law and Policy is a prominent academic and research program in technology law and policy, comprising twenty faculty, staff, and students. The Institute houses interdisciplinary research projects of significant reach and impact. It is funded by public and private funders including government funding agencies, nonprofit foundations, and private donors. It coordinates a Tech Law Scholars program for JD students and oversees the Georgetown Law Technology Review, an active and well-read student-run and faculty-advised publication, and it publishes white papers, policy briefs, and other products of its faculty, staff, and affiliate scholars’ research. It organizes and deepens Georgetown’s programming and curricular efforts in technology-related fields. It coordinates its activities with other Centers and Programs, including the Knight Georgetown Institute, the Center on Privacy and Technology, and the Center on National Security. The institute supports development of affiliated programming and works towards establishing Georgetown Law as a preeminent forum for discussion and study of technology-related legal and policy issues.

The Executive Director develops the structure and programming of the Institute for Technology Law and Policy; works to establish the Institute as a leading voice in and convener of discussions and debates about technology law and policy; spearheads the Institute’s fundraising and communications efforts; collaborates with faculty members to develop research programs and oversees implementation; advises faculty about funding, staffing, and space needs; represents the Institute in high-profile fora and events; builds and maintains connections with University cross-campus collaborations including the Technology & Society Initiative; helps recruit key staff; oversees the publication of research; and supervises the day-to-day functions of Institute staff, fellows, and students.

The Executive Director oversees the Institute budget, including for staff salary, programs, and activities; and facilitates the administration of grant funding on behalf of principal investigators who are affiliated with the Institute.

The Executive Director’s work and duties may require occasional travel.

Work Interactions

Interact with: faculty directors and advisors regarding institution-building, research, and event planning; legal

About GlobalFoundries
GlobalFoundries is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing design, development, and manufacturing services to customers worldwide. Horizon Media, founded in 1989 by Bill Koenigsberg, is recognized as one of the most innovative marketing and advertising firms. We are headquartered in New York City, with offices in Los Angeles and Toronto. A leader in driving business solutions for marketers, Horizon is known for its highly personal approach to client service. The Director of Enterprise Data Governance reports to the SVP of Data Governance, Privacy & Risk. This role is responsible for implementing and operating Horizon’s enterprise data governance program.

- Establish and maintain clear, actionable enterprise data governance policies, standards, and guidelines that convert legal and regulatory requirements into operational business rules.
- Partner closely with Legal and Information Security teams to ensure data governance policies seamlessly align with client contractual commitments.
- Provide strategic, policy-level guidance to business units on how to safely activate client and third-party data under specific contractual parameters.

Data Governance Transformation
- Develop and maintain the governance standards, data inventory guidelines, and Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) frameworks required to support Horizon’s strategic evolution from a Data Processor to Limited Data Controller.

insightsoftware is a global provider of reporting, analytics, and performance management solutions that unlock the potential of business data and transform the way finance and data teams operate. About the Role:
Reporting to the Executive Director of Program Management, the Senior Director of Program Management will be responsible and accountable for the coordination and leadership of activities associated with advancing novel Neurology and Other Rare Disease gene therapy programs through late-stage clinical development, regulatory approval, and into commercial launch. While the primary focus of this role is late-stage development — spanning pivotal trials, regulatory submission, and launch readiness — the individual may also provide program management support to earlier-stage programs within the gene therapy portfolio as needs evolve.

The Sr. Director of Program Management will serve as the operational COO for the Global Program Team (GPT), utilizing best-in-class program management capabilities to provide end-to-end oversight of program strategy and execution — including initiating, planning, executing, controlling, reporting, and closing integrated Program and Functional development plans across the Neurology and Rare Disease therapeutic area.

As a senior operational leader, the Sr. Director of PM will provide cross-functional operational and program management leadership, strategic thinking, and business acumen for late-stage gene therapy programs in a matrixed R&D organization. This individual will bring a commercialization mindset to development planning, ensuring that regulatory strategy, market access, and launch readiness are integrated into the program from the outset of late-stage development.

Additionally, the Sr. Director of PM will work with the PM team and global organization to design and refine processes and business structures, recommending solutions that drive process standardization and simplification across the company.

** This role will ideally be filled with someone local to our San Diego Office or located on the west coast. Candidates in other locations will be considered if willing to travel as needed.
What You'll Do:
In this role, you will serve as the operational COO for the Global Program Team (GPT), partnering with the GPT Head to drive strategy execution, align cross-functional priorities, and ensure the program team operates with clarity, accountability, and urgency through pivotal trials, regulatory submission, approval, and commercial launch.

Director of Security, Property Management
What this job involves:
As Director of Security, Property Management, you will take ownership of the safety and security strategy for a portfolio of properties, ensuring that every tenant, visitor, and team member feels protected and valued. You will design, implement, and continuously refine security programs that balance rigorous risk management with a welcoming, service-oriented environment. This role calls for a leader who can translate complex regulatory and risk considerations into practical, day-to-day operations, while building strong relationships with the client, and local authorities.
What your day-to-day will look like:
- Service as the security liaison with the client’s security team, CTA, and relevant stakeholders
- Develop and maintain comprehensive security plans, protocols, and emergency response procedures tailored to each property's risk profile.
- Conduct regular security assessments and audits, identifying vulnerabilities and recommending practical, cost-effective improvements.
- Oversee contracted security vendors and in-house security staff, ensuring performance meets JLL and client standards.
- Partner closely with property management teams, clients, and local law enforcement to build trusted, collaborative relationships.
- Manage security budgets, procurement of equipment and services, and vendor contract negotiations.
- Lead incident response and investigations, documenting findings and implementing corrective actions.
- Monitor industry trends, emerging threats, and regulatory changes to keep security strategies current and effective.
- Deliver training programs that build staff awareness and readiness around safety, security, and emergency procedures.
- Report on security performance metrics and present recommendations to senior leadership and clients.

This leader will shape how AI, data, and engineering automation accelerate the full technology and product development lifecycle.

You will own three foundational areas: an AI-ready enterprise data platform grounded in knowledge graphs and ontology, modern CI/CD and developer platforms, and source-control modernization. As a key member of the AI leadership team, you will build a high-performing global organization and deliver measurable business outcomes for engineering and product teams.

- Define and execute the ITP AI data platform vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap, including enterprise data products, knowledge graphs, semantic layers, ontology, data pipelines, metadata, lineage, and governance.

- Build, lead, and develop a global organization of data engineers, knowledge engineers, platform and DevOps engineers, and architects, with a strong focus on succession and leadership development.
- Partner with Product Engineering, Technology Development, Business Units, IT, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Architecture, Legal, and strategic technology partners to align platform strategy with business priorities.
- Manage platform budgets, vendor relationships, and technology portfolios, and represent the platform strategy in executive reviews and architecture forums.

Minimum Qualifications
- Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field.
- 20+ years of progressive experience in software engineering, data platforms, developer platforms, DevOps, or AI/ML platforms, including 10+ years leading senior technical teams, managers, and architects.

About the role
We are seeking a senior, hands-on Senior Engineer with a strong backend Java/python focus to join IBD & GCM Technology, part of the wider Institutional Securities Technology (IST) Division. The team supports the complex and evolving needs of two of the firm's most prestigious and market-leading businesses, Investment Banking and Global Capital Markets.

This role combines deep technical expertise with people leadership. You will lead a group of engineers, set technical direction for your area, and act as a primary technology partner to the business. The Company

PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards.  Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day.  We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

Build AI That Could Help Transform the Future of Medicine

Frontier AI is changing what’s possible in science, and few places let you apply it to a problem as consequential as human health. Pfizer is one of them. We have decades of world-class biology and chemistry, rich biomedical data and the global reach to get medicines to patients. We are pairing them with the newest advances in AI and we are doing it along with the world’s leaders in building medicine.

At Pfizer, we believe the next generation of scientific breakthroughs will be powered by advances in artificial intelligence. From foundation models and multimodal learning to biological reasoning and agentic systems, AI has the potential to fundamentally change how we discover, develop, and deliver medicines to patients.  You will help create the scientific foundations behind that future at Pfizer.

We are not looking for one clever model for one clever problem or applying existing models to a single problem. You will develop, extend, and rigorously evaluate advanced AI methods that generate new scientific insights, accelerate experimentation, and enable better decision-making across the drug discovery and development lifecycle. We are building AI that compounds. A method, benchmark or model that works in one disease area should become a foundation that can impact across oncology, immunology/inflammation, internal medicine, vaccines and beyond. You’ll design for that!

Working alongside world-class AI researchers, computational biologists, engineers, and domain experts, you'll tackle some of the most challenging and meaningful problems in healthcare while building technology that has the potential to impact millions of patients worldwide.

Why This Role Is Different
Own Meaningful Scientific Challenges: You will own defined model components, benchmarks, evaluation frameworks, and research workflows that directly influence how AI is applied across Pfizer's R&D organization. You'll build the models, and you'll also decide whether they create real scientific value and whether that value holds up in new contexts.

Where you will push the frontier:  You'll contribute to cutting-edge research across areas such as:

-
- Foundation models and representation learning.
- Multimodal learning across molecular, imaging, clinical and omics data
- Agentic AI and scientific reasoning systems
- Biological Sequence & Structure Modeling
- Graph learning and knowledge graphs
- Clinical & Real-World Data Modeling
- Uncertainty-Aware AI, causal ML and Interpretability

Create Impact Beyond Research Papers
Publishing matters, but the goal is bigger. Your work will help scientists understand disease biology, prioritize experiments, and evaluate therapeutic opportunities across the portfolio. It will speed up medicines for the people waiting on them.

Work at the frontier, with the people who can ship it to patients.

At Quickbase, we help organizations build better ways to run their operations. Our products give teams the flexibility to create applications around how their work actually happens, connecting people, information, and processes so they can keep work moving as needs change.

For more than 25 years, organizations have turned to Quickbase to solve operational challenges that off-the-shelf software wasn't built for. Today, we’re building on that foundation with new products and new possibilities for how people create, adapt, and improve the systems their work depends on.

Job Title : Director, Systems Architecture and Modernization

The Mandate
Quickbase's Core systems weren't built for what comes next. Every AI workflow, every agentic capability, every attempt to let people outside ETE build against our data runs into the same wall: systems that are tightly coupled, hard to decouple, and carrying years of technical debt.
This role exists to tear that wall down. You will lead the people who build and maintain Core Architecture and Systems Engineering, reduce the debt in systems like Salesforce, and make headless real at Quickbase — our systems exposing clean APIs instead of forcing every integration through custom logic. That is the precondition for everything else ETE is building, including the Builder platform that will let the business build AI workflows without waiting on ETE.
You will also own the technical direction for the biggest systems project ETE will run this cycle: rebuilding our Core Quoting and Billing infrastructure.

Team Leadership
- Lead the combined Core Architecture and Systems Engineering teams — architects and Salesforce/systems engineers
- Set the technical bar for the people who build and maintain the systems Quickbase's revenue motion runs on
- You are accountable for the outcome. You do not chair a review committee. You make the call and document it.
Systems Modernization & Technical Debt
- Own the reduction of technical debt in Salesforce and adjacent Core systems: fewer custom flows, less undocumented logic, a system that can actually be reasoned about
- Define and drive the headless architecture strategy — decouple Core systems behind clean APIs so they can be consumed safely by any system, human, or agent that needs them, not just the ones built to know their internals
- Partner with the Sr. Manager of Systems Management on platform health and technical debt prioritization

workday:see's candies:JR107237.description:
Work is Sweet!

'Quality without Compromise' is not just a motto at See’s Candies. It is the most important ingredient in our recipe for success. See’s Candies has been in business since 1921 and maintains a reputation for producing the highest quality candy and providing superior customer service.

See’s is a leader in the confectionery industry with over 250 retail shops across the USA, a growing e-commerce business, and expanding opportunities internationally. We are seeking friendly, enthusiastic individuals who are passionate about helping us grow and thrive in our second century.

Job Description Summary:
The purpose of this position is to develop and direct the Engineering function for See’s manufacturing and packing operations in five facilities in Los Angeles and San Francisco/Bay Area CA. The role is responsible for long term planning, capital budgeting, project design, installation and supplier relationships. The role directly manages the Engineering group and works closely with plant maintenance, Quality Assurance, Research and Development, Information Technology, and Finance on design, financial control and implementation.

The pay range for this position is expected to be $220,000k -$250,000 annually; however, base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.
Job Description:

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Responsible for life-cycle management and total equipment cost of processing and packaging equipment in five locations in the San Francisco/Bay Area and Los Angeles, California.
- Evaluates existing environment, equipment, condition, safety, utilization, operating cost and ability to meet current & future business needs.  Based on above and knowledge of supplier and equipment market, recommends modifications, replacements and expansions through capital budgeting process.
- Owns capital budgeting and project execution process for processing and packaging equipment.  Coordinates all information, including complete ROI or other analysis to ensure accurate fiscal budget is prepared and presented along with a five-year development plan indicating longer term capital requirements.  Follows and helps to improve approval and financial control processes.
- Oversees and/or manages execution of individual projects coordinating assignments to line managed Engineering team members and plant managed maintenance team members ensuring project management processes include all stakeholders (plants, QA, Finance etc.).  Ensures delivery of projects on time, on scope and on budget through startup support and handover to plants.  Escalates project and supplier issues as needed.
- Leads detailed monthly project status reviews including KPIs and project timeline status with Senior Management.
- Able to understand and develop technology utilization to support efficient and progressive improvement of confection production.  Works closely with Information Technolo

The ISR (Intelligence, Surveillance & Reconnaissance), Aviation, and Security (IAS) business area is a leader in ISR and aviation, it is a leading prime manned and unmanned aircraft systems integrator for innovative, high-performance ISR and aviation systems. Its end-to-end Command, Control, Computers, Communications and Intelligence, Surveillance & Reconnaissance (C4ISR) capabilities encompass design, integration, test, certification, ground/flight training and complete logistics support. IAS tailors solutions to customer cost, performance, and schedule requirements and designs to consistently exceed expectations – with an unrivaled record of on time and on (or under) budget deliveries.

SNC has led thoughtful and disruptive change in the aerospace and defense industry for the past 60 years and now, we’re applying this tenacity and expertise to the U.S. Air Force’s (USAF) Survivable Airborne Operations Center (SAOC) mission. Join the SNC-led SAOC team and be a part of exciting and meaningful work to modernize and deliver the next-generation SAOC aircraft trusted by the President, Secretary of Defense and Chairs of the Joint Chiefs of Staff to ensure continued critical command, control and communication during national emergencies. If you’re passionate about building the airborne command post of the future, consider SNC for your next mission. Learn more about NC3 and SAOC here .

Are you looking to advance your career and flex your leadership and program management skills in a fast-paced and rewarding organization? Join us! The Director Programs will lead strategic business operations for key programmatic aspects at SNC. This role requires a visionary leader responsible for overseeing customer relationships, cost management, schedule adherence, technical planning, and execution. The Director Programs will ensure program performance objectives are achieved through meticulous tracking and reporting, risk assessment, and resolution of issues. This position involves close coordination with corporate entities, fostering innovation, and deploying complex solutions in a mission-critical environment. The incumbent will be responsible for providing program status updates, reviewing proposals, and negotiating with stakeholders to ensure that projects meet financial and timeline constraints.

Sierra Space Careers:
At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.

Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.

Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.

We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.

About the Role
Sierra Space is scaling from development programs into high-rate, repeatable production across a diversified portfolio of military and commercial systems, including satellites and spacecraft, propulsion systems, solar power systems, and the Dream Chaser spaceplane. As Director, Production Operations based in Madison, Wisconsin, you will play a critical role in executing the production strategy for propulsion development and manufacturing, building the operational systems required to deliver hardware at pace, at quality, and at cost.

This is an execution-focused leadership role for a proven operations professional with expertise in propulsion systems. Reporting to the Vice President, Production, you will lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines and additional enterprise products within Sierra Space's Madison facility. You will drive standardization of production processes, implement data-driven manufacturing systems, and build high-performing teams capable of scaling propulsion output while maintaining quality and efficiency. You will partner closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Program Management to ensure production readiness and on-time delivery of critical propulsion systems for space and defense applications.

Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission.

We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

About SiFive

As the pioneers who introduced RISC-V to the world, SiFive is transforming the future of compute by bringing the limitless potential of RISC-V to the highest performance and most data-intensive applications in the world. SiFive’s unrivaled compute platforms are continuing to enable leading technology companies around the world to innovate, optimize and deliver the most advanced solutions of tomorrow across every market segment of chip design, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, automotive, data center, mobile, and consumer. With SiFive, the future of RISC-V has no limits.

At SiFive, we are always excited to connect with talented individuals, who are just as passionate about driving innovation and changing the world as we are.

Our constant innovation and ongoing success is down to our amazing teams of incredibly talented people, who collaborate and support each other to come up with truly groundbreaking ideas and solutions.  Solutions that will have a huge impact on people's lives; making the world a better place, one processor at a time.

Are you ready?

To learn more about SiFive’s phenomenal success and to see why we have won the   GSA’s prestigious Most Respected Private Company Award   (for the fourth time!), check out our   website   and   Glassdoor   pages.

Job Description:

We are seeking a technically strong Sr Directorr of Software Product Management to define and drive the software products and developer experiences that enable customers to successfully deploy our semiconductor IP for our datacenter compute product portfolio.

This role is responsible for translating the needs of hyperscalars, chip designers, software developers, system architects, end customers and the open source community into a coherent software strategy.

You will work across product management, architecture, engineering, applications, sales, marketing, and external ecosystem partners to make our IP easy to evaluate, integrate, program, validate, and deploy in production systems.

The ideal candidate understands both software development, Customer deployment needs and semiconductor development cycles. You can discuss developer workflows and APIs with software teams, while also understanding how firmware, toolchains, operating systems, hardware features, and silicon schedules interact.

This person will:
- Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for software products supporting our semiconductor IP portfolio for our datacenter compute portfolio of products
- Define requirements for SDKs, toolchains, compilers, debuggers, simulators, firmware, board-support packages, drivers, middleware, operating-system enablement, and developer tools.
- Develop a deep understanding of customer workflows, including IP evaluation, SoC integration, software porting, bring-up, validation, performance optimization, and production deployment.
- Engage directly with customers, partners, and software developers to identify pain points, validate produ

• Solid understanding of reliability engineering, including developing reliability plans for product development, accelerated life testing design and analysis, reliability analysis and prediction

• Persistent, driven, self-motivated, keen to make an impact
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills

State Street is seeking a Senior Vice President, Head of Technology, Wealth Services . The SVP will set and execute the technology vision for Wealth Services, with end-to-end accountability for architecture, engineering, platform delivery, operational resilience, cybersecurity, data, and strategic partner integration across State Street’s Wealth Custody & Clearing business. The role will shape enterprise investment priorities and lead to the modernization and scaling of custody, clearing, advisor, and client platforms through a cloud-native, API-first strategy.

Why This Role is important to us
Wealth Services Technology is building State Street’s next-generation wealth platform, spanning broker-dealer, custody, clearing, advisor, and digital client capabilities. The organization operates at the intersection of business strategy, technology transformation, regulatory accountability, and strategic partnerships.

This role is accountable for establishing the technology direction, governance, operating model, and execution discipline required to deliver secure, resilient, and scalable solutions. The SVP will influence enterprise strategy, advise senior executives, and align technology investment to growth, client, risk, and financial outcomes. The position is critical to expanding the business, protecting the franchise, and delivering differentiated capabilities to institutional and RIA clients.
What you will be responsible for

As a Senior Vice President, you will:
- Set and execute the multi-year Wealth Services technology strategy and target architecture, aligning priorities with business growth, client commitments, enterprise standards, and risk appetite.
- Own the Wealth Services technology portfolio including, but not limited to, the following: investment roadmap, operating plan, and financial performance, including prioritization, funding decisions, benefits realization, vendor spend, and cost optimization.
- Provide executive sponsorship for the design and delivery of a scalable, cloud-native platform supporting account opening, trading, clearing, settlement, custody, portfolio accounting, compliance, and reporting.
- Establish architecture and engineering standards, including API-first, event-driven, data, cybersecurity, and resilience patterns that enable secure integration and real-time processing.
- Lead the technology strategy and executive governance for third-party clearing and custody relationships with clear accountability for delivery, service levels, controls, concentration risk, and commercial outcomes.
- Chair or represent technology in senior governance forums, providing transparent reporting, decisive escalation, and recommendations on delivery, operational, cyber, regulatory, and third-party risks.
- Ensure the technology environment meets applicable regulatory and control expectations including, but not limited to, SEC, FINRA, AML, KYC, OFAC, privacy, cybersecurity, records management, and operational resilience requirements

Recent advancements in underlying technology have finally made it possible for AI to impact clinical care in a meaningful way. Passionate about precision medicine and advancing the healthcare industry?
Recent advancements in underlying technology have finally made it possible for AI to impact clinical care in a meaningful way. Tempus' proprietary platform connects an entire ecosystem of real-world evidence to deliver real-time, actionable insights to physicians, providing critical information about the right treatments for the right patients, at the right time.

All of that depends on data moving reliably and at scale: real-time clinical messages streaming in from health systems, petabyte-scale batch backfills, and datasets shared with partners. Data Platform builds the systems that move healthcare data into and out of Tempus, and we are making that platform self-service, so any team at Tempus can ingest, transform, and share data on its own, with data governance built in so every dataset carries the usage rules that apply to it.

We are looking for a Senior Director of Software Engineering to lead our Data Platform engineering organization, set its technical direction, and report to the Chief Data Technology Officer.

The Team
Data Platform is organized as small, autonomous pods. Each pod owns a clear system domain and partners with a dedicated product manager:
- Edge Compute: Builds, packages, and operates a fleet of on-premises appliances deployed inside health systems, along with a growing catalog of connectors to on-premises clinical systems for batch and real-time use cases. The pod manages fleet health at scale and is opening the edge so other Tempus teams can deploy their own workloads there.
- Gateways & Processing: Runs the high-throughput, secure cloud gateways (FHIR APIs and large-scale file transfer) that partners use to send messages and files, and the processing tools that map, enrich, and validate that data. The goal is that 100% of incoming data is application-ready, standardized FHIR, delivered through integration patterns that serve both people and machines.
- Pipeline Orchestration: Builds event-driven pipelines and a workflow orchestration platform with robust error handling, logging, and repair, so clinical workflows run reliably at scale. The pod also owns egress, letting data owners define how their data is packaged and delivered, and tracks every message through its full lifecycle.

About Us

At Transamerica, hard work, innovative thinking, and personal accountability are qualities we honor and reward. We understand the potential of leveraging the talents of a diverse workforce. We embrace an environment where employees enjoy a balance between their careers, families, communities, and personal interests.

Ultimately, we appreciate the uniqueness of a company where talented professionals work collaboratively in a positive environment — one focused on helping people look forward and plan for the best life possible while providing tools and solutions that make it easier to get there.

Who We Are

We believe everyone deserves to live their best life. More than a century ago, we were among the first financial services companies in America to serve everyday people from all walks of life .

Today, we’re part of an international holding company, with millions of customers and thousands of employees worldwide. Our insurance, retirement, and investment solutions help people make the most of what’s important to them.

We’re empowered by a vast agent network covering North America, with diversity to match. Together with our nonprofit research institute and foundation, we tune in, step up, and are a force for good — for our customers and the communities where we live, work, and play. United in our purpose, we help people create the financial freedom to live life on their terms.

These are supported by Transamerica Corporate , which includes Finance, People and Places, General Counsel, Risk, Internal Audit, Strategy and Development, and Corporate Affairs, which covers Communications, Brand, and Government and Policy Affairs.

Transamerica employs nearly 7 ,000 people. It’s part of Aegon, an integrated, diversified, international financial services group serving approximately 23.9 million customers worldwide. * For more information, visit transamerica.com .

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That’s the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

$123,400.00 - $203,600.00

1
What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers is seeking a Director, Technical Product Owner to work with the teams in the AI & Engineering Enablement circle within Claim Technology's Engineering Enablement group. The circle exists to build an AI-native software delivery system for Claim. It reshapes how engineers work alongside AI, automates the toil around delivery, codifies reusable patterns and standards, and gives clear insight into delivery health.
Your customers are Claim's engineers, engineering leaders and enterprise technology groups. You will help intake and prioritize work from these groups, managing relationships and staying true to the Engineering Enablement pillars. You will partner with the Enablement Lead and Circle Leads to set strategy and priorities, then own execution with the teams. You will focus on outcomes, like shorter lead time and real adoption, rather than how the work gets done. Azure is now the home of World Finance's core business systems, and the company will keep building there. The Director of IT Cloud Operations owns the Azure platform as a managed program: setting the strategy, designing the target architecture, and leading the execution that moves the environment from one built one resource at a time to a governed, secure-by-default cloud. The Director leads a small, high-leverage team, draws on the wider IT organization and external delivery partners, and is accountable for where the cloud is headed and how well it runs along the way.
This is a player-coach seat. In a given week the Director may set the quarter's roadmap with IT leadership, review a landing-zone design and a pipeline change from the team, pair on an infrastructure-as-code module, work through a remediation plan with Information Security, and manage an external partner's delivery. The role requires both leadership and hands-on depth.

Establish a scored maturity model with a named owner for each capability, reassess at least annually, and use the gaps to shape the platform roadmap and report progress to IT leadership.
- Own the environment cleanup already underway: retire orphaned and idle resources, close platform-level exposures, and turn point-in-time findings into a routed, SLA-backed remediation flow.

- Set the multi-year cloud direction and own the target state including landing zones, networking, identity and secrets strategy, and cloud standards.

- Run cloud spend as a managed number through tagging, right-sizing, reservations, lifecycle controls, and reporting.
- Establish prioritization, documentation, review gates, and audit evidence supporting SOX ITGC, GLBA/FTC Safeguards, and PCI DSS.
- Ensure monitoring, backup standards, logging, and remediation of platform-level posture findings.
- Other duties as assigned.
